replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a second-order equation: 1) Identify coefficients (ax² + bx + c = 0). 2) Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). 3) If positive, use the quadratic formula to find two real roots. 4) Plug values into (-b ± sqrt(discriminant)) / 2a.

To find stationary points: 1) Differentiate the function f(x) to get dy/dx. 2) Set the derivative equal to zero (dy/dx = 0). 3) Solve for x values. 4) Substitute these x values back into original f(x) to find corresponding y coordinates.
